raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Downstream consumers written in Go, Python, and other languages (such as `llm-d/llm-d-router` for `sglang.api.v1.SglangService`) currently have to copy `.proto` files out of `sgl-project/sglang` and maintain local `protoc` pipelines to generate client/message bindings.

Publishing `proto/` as `buf.build/sgl-project/sglang` on the Buf Schema Registry (BSR) lets downstream projects import versioned generated SDKs directly (for example `go get buf.build/gen/go/sgl-project/sglang/protocolbuffers/go` and `buf.build/gen/go/sgl-project/sglang/grpc/go` via BSR Managed Mode) without adding language-specific options like `option go_package` to the `.proto` sources, while enforcing `buf build`, `buf lint`, and `buf breaking` checks on `.proto` changes in CI.

## Modifications

- Add `proto/buf.yaml` (Buf v2) declaring module `buf.build/sgl-project/sglang` with `STANDARD` lint rules (excluding the four naming rules that conflict with existing `sglang.api.v1`, `sglang.json.v1`, and `sglang.runtime.v1` wire contracts) and `FILE` breaking-change detection.
- Add `proto/README.md`, rendered by the BSR as the module documentation: generated SDK usage, version labels, a warning that the SDKs target the gRPC wire format (the HTTP JSON form follows the `sglang.json.v1` options, not canonical proto3 JSON), and the schema change process.
- Add `.github/workflows/buf.yml` (Buf CLI pinned to 1.75.0):
  - On pull requests touching `proto/**`: `buf build`, `buf lint`, and `buf breaking` against the PR's base commit. A maintainer can approve an intentional breaking change with the `buf skip breaking` label, which re-triggers the check.
  - On `main` pushes, `v*` release tag pushes, published GitHub releases, and manual dispatch on `main`: publish `proto/` to the BSR, labeled with the commit SHA and the branch or tag name.
  - Before publishing from `main`, re-run `buf breaking` against the previous `main` commit unless the merged PR carries `buf skip breaking`. The PR check is not a required status check, so this keeps an unapproved breaking change out of the registry.
  - Publishing is opt-in via `vars.BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED`, so this can merge before the registry is set up. Once enabled, a missing `BUF_TOKEN` fails the job instead of silently skipping.

## Maintainer setup (after merge)

1. Create the `sgl-project` organization on buf.build (`buf push --create` creates the module, not the organization).
2. Create a BSR token for a bot or service account in that organization and add it as the `BUF_TOKEN` repository secret.
3. Set the `BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED` repository variable to `true`.
4. Run the "Buf Protobuf" workflow manually on `main` once for the first publish.
5. Create the `buf skip breaking` label.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A (protobuf build/CI configuration only; no runtime or model changes).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A (protobuf build/CI configuration only).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+name: Buf Protobuf
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    tags:
+      - "v[0-9]+.*"
+    paths:
+      - "proto/**"
+      - ".github/workflows/buf.yml"
+  release:
+    types:
+      - published
+  pull_request:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]
+    paths:
+      - "proto/**"
+      - ".github/workflows/buf.yml"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+concurrency:
+  group: buf-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  # Read the merged PR's labels before publishing a push to main.
+  pull-requests: read
+
+jobs:
+  buf:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout code
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Set up Buf
+        uses: bufbuild/buf-action@v1
+        with:
+          version: 1.75.0
+          setup_only: true
+
+      - name: Build and lint protobuf schemas
+        run: |
+          buf build proto
+          buf lint proto
+
+      - name: Check for breaking protobuf changes
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'buf skip breaking')
+        env:
+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+        run: |
+          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "${BASE_SHA}"
+          base_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
+          trap 'rm -rf "${base_dir}"' EXIT
+          git archive "${BASE_SHA}" proto | tar -x -C "${base_dir}"
+          buf breaking proto --against "${base_dir}/proto"
+
+      # The PR check is not a required status check, so a PR whose breaking
+      # check failed can still merge. Re-check against the previous main commit
+      # so an unapproved breaking change never reaches the registry.
+      - name: Block unapproved breaking changes before publishing
+        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
+        run: |
+          labels="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${GITHUB_SHA}/pulls" --jq '.[].labels[].name')"
+          if grep -qxF 'buf skip breaking' <<<"${labels}"; then
+            echo "::notice::Breaking changes approved via the 'buf skip breaking' label."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "${BEFORE_SHA}"
+          base_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
+          trap 'rm -rf "${base_dir}"' EXIT
+          git archive "${BEFORE_SHA}" proto | tar -x -C "${base_dir}"
+          buf breaking proto --against "${base_dir}/proto"
+
+      - name: Push module to Buf Schema Registry
+        if: (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'release' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')) && github.repository == 'sgl-project/sglang'
+        env:
+          BUF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BUF_TOKEN }}
+          BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED: ${{ vars.BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED }}
+        run: |
+          # Publishing is opt-in so this workflow can merge before the registry
+          # is set up; once enabled, a missing token fails instead of skipping.
+          if [ "${BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED}" != "true" ]; then
+            echo "::notice::Skipping BSR push because vars.BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED is not 'true'."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          if [ -z "${BUF_TOKEN}" ]; then
+            echo "::error::vars.BSR_PUBLISH_ENABLED is 'true' but secrets.BUF_TOKEN is empty."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          labels=(--label "${GITHUB_SHA}")
+          if [ -n "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" ]; then
+            labels+=(--label "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
+          fi
+          buf push proto \
+            --create \
+            --create-visibility public \
+            --create-default-label main \
+            --source-control-url "${GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commit/${GITHUB_SHA}" \
+            "${labels[@]}"

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# SGLang protobuf schemas
+
+The protobuf definitions of SGLang's gRPC APIs. CI publishes this directory to
+the Buf Schema Registry as
+[`buf.build/sgl-project/sglang`](https://buf.build/sgl-project/sglang).
+
+| Package | Contents |
+|---------|----------|
+| `sglang.api.v1` | The native `SglangService` gRPC API, which shares its request and response messages with the HTTP API. |
+| `sglang.json.v1` | Custom options that define the HTTP JSON form of `sglang.api.v1` messages. |
+| `sglang.runtime.v1` | The gRPC bridge protocol. |
+
+## Generated SDKs
+
+Use the [generated SDKs](https://buf.build/sgl-project/sglang/sdks) instead of
+copying these files. For example, in Go:
+
+```bash
+go get buf.build/gen/go/sgl-project/sglang/protocolbuffers/go@vX.Y.Z
+go get buf.build/gen/go/sgl-project/sglang/grpc/go@vX.Y.Z
+```
+
+Each published commit is labeled with its Git commit SHA. Commits on `main`
+are also labeled `main`, and release tags are labeled with their tag name (for
+example `v0.5.24`). Pin a release tag or commit SHA rather than `main`.
+
+## gRPC wire format only
+
+The generated SDKs are meant for gRPC (the binary protobuf wire format). The
+HTTP JSON form of these messages is **not** the canonical proto3 JSON mapping:
+the `sglang.json.v1` options change it (bare lists, positional tuples,
+scalar-or-list unions, embedded raw JSON). Do not use `protojson` or
+`json_format` on these types to build or parse SGLang HTTP request and
+response bodies.
+
+## Changing the schemas
+
+- `buf lint` and `buf breaking` (the `FILE` rules in `buf.yaml`) run on every
+  pull request that touches this directory.
+- A deliberate breaking change needs maintainer sign-off: a maintainer applies
+  the `buf skip breaking` label to the pull request. The same check runs again
+  before publishing from `main`, and it honors the same label.
+- The checked-in Rust and Python bindings are generated from these files. After
+  editing a `.proto` file, run `cd rust && cargo gen-api` and commit the
+  regenerated output with the schema change.

@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+version: v2
+name: buf.build/sgl-project/sglang
+lint:
+  use:
+    - STANDARD
+  except:
+    # Existing wire schemas use domain-specific response/stream names
+    # (e.g., GenerateStreamItem, HiCacheStatus) and shared response messages.
+    - ENUM_ZERO_VALUE_SUFFIX
+    - RPC_REQUEST_RESPONSE_UNIQUE
+    - RPC_REQUEST_STANDARD_NAME
+    - RPC_RESPONSE_STANDARD_NAME
+breaking:
+  use:
+    - FILE
